o: Keys lie on three rows laid out vertically: qwertyuiop (row 0), asdfghjkl (row 1), zxcvbnm (row 2), each column = index within its row. Starting at 'a' = (1,0), sum Manhattan distances between consecutive characters of s. For 'hello': 5 + 4 + 7 + 0 + 1 = 17.
k: Flatten the three rows into one string; row = index // 10, column = index % 10.
Answer is the sum of Manhattan distances along the path, starting from 'a'.

a.n: Approach 1: Precomputed positions and a single pass
a.i: Map every letter to (row, col) once, then walk the string accumulating |dr| + |dc| between successive keys.
s: Build the position table from the concatenated layout string.
For each character, add the Manhattan distance to its position and move there.
a.sp: O(1) — the position table is fixed size.

w: Pure simulation; the only risks are mis-transcribing the layout (note 'asdfghjkl' has 9 keys, so column indices shift per row) and forgetting the finger starts on 'a' rather than costing a move to it. A natural follow-up asks for two fingers minimizing total distance — that becomes a much harder DP.
